relevant_findings.topic: Deck RP inherits NC coating_type as primary dimension — NOT quality_tier
relevant_findings.content: The NC deck spec (SF_DECK_EXT_v1) established coating_type as the primary configuration dimension replacing quality_tier. The RP spec inherits this structure. Coating_type drives: coating chemistry (penetrating vs film-forming), maintenance cycle, failure mode profile, primer requirement for solid stain re-coating, coat count, and material coverage rates. The RP spec adds an existing coating assessment dimension that the NC spec does not need.

relevant_findings.topic: Deck RP adds condition assessment as mandatory first step — mirrors trim RP pattern
relevant_findings.content: Unlike NC deck work, repaint/restain requires condition assessment before committing to prep strategy. Following the SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1 pattern: ASTM D3359 adhesion test on existing coating, existing coating type identification (solvent wipe test: denatured alcohol dissolves latex, not oil), DSD-equivalent assessment for existing stain condition, and rot probe at vulnerable locations (stair treads, end grain, posts at grade contact). Assessment is a FIXED time module — not area-dependent. Assessment determines: (a) whether to strip or sand-and-recoat, (b) coating compatibility, (c) structural repair referrals.

relevant_findings.topic: Existing coating stripping is the dominant RP prep task — dwarfs NC prep
relevant_findings.content: Previously coated decks with failing stain/paint require full chemical strip + brightener + rinse cycle. This is the same chemical restoration protocol from the NC spec (MOD_DECK_CHEMICAL_RESTORE) but activated by existing coating failure rather than weathering. Key difference from NC: RP stripping must contend with unknown existing coating chemistry. Oil-based stains require different strippers than water-based. Epoxy-fortified coatings may resist standard strippers. When existing coating is sound, RP can skip stripping entirely and apply over existing (compatibility permitting). This creates a wide prep labor variance — from light scuff sand (sound existing, same product) to full chemical strip + 24-48 hr dry (failing existing, unknown product).
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Decks_Horizontal_Wood_Doctrine.md maintenance cycles; SF_DECK_EXT_v1 chemical restoration module

relevant_findings.topic: Substrate state inputs for deck RP are stain-specific — different from paint RP
relevant_findings.content: The NC deck spec outputs SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI (penetrating stains) or SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID (film-forming solid stain). Deck RP must accept BOTH as input states, plus SS_EXT_WEATHERED for decks that have lost their previous coating through UV degradation. SS_EXT_PAINTED_FLAT and SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN are also valid inputs — some decks were previously painted with porch floor enamel (not stained). This gives 5 valid input states: SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI, SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID, SS_EXT_WEATHERED, SS_EXT_PAINTED_FLAT, SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN.

relevant_findings.topic: Coating compatibility matrix is critical — wrong combination causes delamination
relevant_findings.content: Deck RP coating compatibility is more complex than paint RP because stains and paints have fundamentally different adhesion mechanisms. Key rules: (1) Penetrating stain over penetrating stain = safe, stain absorbs into wood through existing. (2) Solid stain over penetrating stain = safe, film-forming over penetrating substrate. (3) Penetrating stain over solid stain = FAIL, cannot penetrate through film. (4) Oil-based over water-based = generally safe. (5) Water-based over oil-based = RISKY, adhesion testing mandatory. (6) Paint over stain = requires bonding primer. (7) Stain over paint = FAIL unless fully stripped. Assessment module determines existing coating type to select compatible re-coating strategy.

relevant_findings.topic: RP deck uses QT2-QT3 range — utilitarian surface with functional finish
relevant_findings.content: Deck staining is utilitarian — foot traffic surface with limited aesthetic expectation compared to trim or siding. QT2 = maintenance recoat (single coat, minimal prep, no inspection). QT3 = standard refinish (full prep, 2 coats, final inspection). QT4/QT5 excluded — deck staining does not warrant premium/gallery quality treatment. Coating_type remains the primary dimension; quality_tier is secondary, controlling coat count and inspection rigor.
relevant_findings.source: SF_DECK_EXT_v1 spec context; PaintFactor OS quality tier definitions

relevant_findings.topic: Deck RP adds existing coating condition dimension — drives prep module selection
relevant_findings.content: The NC spec uses wood_condition (new, weathered, previously_coated). The RP spec replaces this with existing_coating_condition: sound, worn, failing, peeling. Sound = existing stain/paint is intact, good adhesion, no peeling — light prep and recoat. Worn = high-traffic areas show wear-through to bare wood but coating is still generally adhered — moderate prep, spot-strip worn areas. Failing = widespread adhesion loss, flaking, blistering — chemical strip required. Peeling = sheet delamination (solid stain/paint) — full strip mandatory, separate mobilization day. This maps roughly to the trim RP DSD 0-3 pattern but with deck-specific failure modes.

relevant_findings.topic: Same 4 paintable items as NC spec — floor SF, railing LF, spindle EA, stair EA
relevant_findings.content: Deck RP works on the same physical components as NC: deck floor field (ITM_DECK_FLOOR, SF), railing system (ITM_DECK_RAILING, LF), spindles/balusters (ITM_DECK_SPINDLE, EA), and stair steps (ITM_DECK_STAIR, EA). No new items needed. The RP-specific difference is that each component has its own condition assessment and may have different existing coating states (e.g., floor peeling but railings sound).

relevant_findings.topic: Production rates for RP application are same as NC — stain application rate is product-dependent not surface-history-dependent
relevant_findings.content: Once prep normalizes the surface, stain application rates are the same for RP and NC. The base rates from SF_DECK_EXT_v1/production.json apply: spray_backbrush 275 SF/hr (2-person), brush 125 SF/hr, pad 250 SF/hr, roll 200 SF/hr, railing brush 10 LF/hr, spindle brush 10 EA/hr, stair brush 3 EA/hr. RP prep tasks are slower due to stripping and existing coating removal, but once prepped, application is rate-equivalent to NC. Factor modifiers FAC_DECK_COATING_TYPE and FAC_DECK_SUBSTRATE_TYPE apply unchanged. FAC_DECK_WOOD_CONDITION is replaced by FAC_DKRP_EXISTING_CONDITION for RP-specific prep scaling.

relevant_findings.topic: Chemical restoration module reused from NC with RP-specific activation conditions
relevant_findings.content: The NC spec's MOD_DECK_CHEMICAL_RESTORE (8 tasks: strip apply, dwell, scrub, rinse, brighten apply, dwell, rinse, dry verify) transfers directly to the RP spec. Activation changes from wood_condition=weathered to existing_coating_condition in [failing, peeling]. Same rates, same chemicals, same 24-48 hr dry time between chemical prep and stain application. For RP, stripping may require stronger formulations for multi-layer existing coatings — this is handled by the FAC_DKRP_EXISTING_CONDITION modifier on strip tasks rather than a separate product.

relevant_findings.topic: Scope_components dimension retained — floor_only, floor_and_railings, full_deck
relevant_findings.content: Same scope_components dimension as NC. RP commonly targets floor_only (floor wears first from foot traffic) while railings and stairs may not need recoating. The scope_components dimension activates/deactivates railing, spindle, and stair modules independently.

relevant_findings.topic: Protection zones identical to NC — reuse all 5 zones
relevant_findings.content: Same protection requirements: ext_siding_adjacent (ledger board), ext_below_deck_landscape (elevated decks), ext_hardscape_patio (walkways), ext_deck_furniture_staging (on-deck items), ext_light_fixture (deck-mounted fixtures). No new zones for RP.

relevant_findings.topic: Solid stain delamination risk is HIGHER for RP than NC
relevant_findings.content: Solid stain over existing solid stain on horizontal surfaces has compounding delamination risk — each coat adds film thickness, increasing moisture entrapment. RP with solid stain on a deck floor that already has 2-3 previous coats of solid stain is at extreme risk. Assessment must include total existing film build measurement. If existing film is thick (>10 mil DFT), full strip is mandatory regardless of visible condition. This is an RP-specific risk not present in NC.

relevant_findings.topic: Environmental conditions remain non-estimatable for deck RP — same as NC
relevant_findings.content: Wind, dew point, surface temperature, direct sun — all managed by SOP scheduling, not estimation modifiers. Deck staining is especially sensitive to direct sun causing flash-drying (stain dries on surface before penetrating). This is a process constraint (schedule for early AM or late PM), not an estimatable variable. Per RC-003 from PaintFactor OS.

relevant_findings.topic: Projected task count: ~38-42 tasks across 9 modules
relevant_findings.content: NC spec has 40 tasks across 8 modules. RP adds an assessment module (~5 tasks: condition assessment, adhesion test, coating ID, moisture test, rot probe) and modifies the prep module for existing coating removal. Some NC-only tasks drop (mill glaze sand, seasoning verify). Net projection: 38-42 tasks across 9 modules (setup, assess, prep_floor, prep_railing, chemical_restore, apply_floor, apply_railing, apply_stair, cleanup).
relevant_findings.source: SF_DECK_EXT_v1 sop_module_summary; SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1 assessment module pattern

configuration_dimensions_proposed.notes: PRIMARY DIMENSION — inherited from NC spec. Clear_sealer EXCLUDED from RP — clear sealer is maintenance-only (reapply same product), not a repaint/restain scenario requiring this spec's assessment and prep pipeline. Semi-transparent remains the professional standard (~60% of deck restaining work).

RP-SPECIFIC DIMENSION — replaces NC's wood_condition. Drives prep intensity and chemical restoration activation. Sound = intact existing coating, light prep. Worn = traffic wear, moderate prep. Failing = adhesion loss, chemical strip required. Peeling = sheet delamination, full strip + separate mobilization day.
Inherited from NC spec unchanged. PT pine ~80% of residential decks.
Inherited from NC spec unchanged. Spray-only PROHIBITED for penetrating stains.
Default to floor_only for RP — floor wears first from foot traffic. NC defaults to full_deck for new construction.

research_corrections.corrected_to: Quality_tier is NOT a configuration dimension for deck specs. Coating_type is the primary dimension. QT is implicit: maintenance recoat behavior (minimal prep, single coat) is captured by existing_coating_condition=sound + coating_type=semi_transparent. No separate QT dimension needed — it would create redundant configuration axes.
research_corrections.source: SF_DECK_EXT_v1 established pattern — no quality_tier dimension in deck specs

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions should be estimation modifiers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable — unpredictable at bid time. Excluded per PaintFactor OS RC-003.
